title: BEGINNER LINE DANCE - COWBOY HUSTLE - TUTORIAL!

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Coral breaks down each section of the line dance step-by-step while facing away from the camera so viewers can easily mirror her movements. She speaks in an encouraging and upbeat tone, combining verbal descriptions with counts and foot close-ups.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to Coral and the Cowboy Hustle line dance.
Breakdown of the first part: fan motion and heels/toes.
Breakdown of the second part: step, kick, step, touch.
Breakdown of the third part: grapevine with quarter turn.
Breakdown of the final part: step out and back hops.
Full practice of the dance with counts from the top.

steps_taught.name: Fan motion / Heels and Toes
steps_taught.description: Fan right toe out-in-out-in, then two heels forward and two toes back.

steps_taught.name: Alternating Heels and Toes
steps_taught.description: Right heel forward, right toe back, right heel forward, right toe back.

steps_taught.name: Step Kick Step Touch
steps_taught.description: Step forward right, kick left, step left, touch right toe back. Repeated twice.

steps_taught.name: Grapevine
steps_taught.description: Step right out, step left behind, step right out, touch left next to right.

what_works: Turning around to face away from the camera so students can mirror her footwork
Inserting dedicated close-up shots of footwork during explanations

quotes.text: You're going to start with your weight on your left foot.
Now let's try this all from the top.
And that's pretty much the complicated part of the dance.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands facing away from the camera with weight on left foot, explaining foot positioning.
Close-up shot of cowboy boots demonstrating out-in-out-in toe fan.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: upper body posture during foot movement

evidence_segments.observation: Close-up shot of boots demonstrating step and kick forward.

extraction.distinctive_method: Integrating specific close-up insert cuts of the instructor's boots directly into the explanation of footwork.
